processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching. This is the parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq.
Solution-treated 17Al samples were aged at 575 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching. Aging was performed between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h.

structures.overall_structure: Bulk microstructure of the Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (17Al) alloy after aging at 575 °C for 3 h. The secondary-electron SEM image for this condition shows a uniform grey matrix in which the elongated/needle-like contrast present after 1 h aging at 575 °C is no longer resolved, indicating that the α → β-Mn transformation has progressed substantially at 3 h. For the same alloy the α matrix was reported to be almost completely transformed into β-Mn after aging at 575 °C for 6 h (EBSD, Fig. 5), so the 575 °C/3 h condition lies in a partially-to-fully transformed regime.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
Elastic modulus measured through compressive stress-strain curves

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times, hardness given by the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 575 °C for 3 h (and the other aging conditions)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished with a mixture of 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol; main panels carry a 50 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in the aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 3 h the SE image shows a uniform grey matrix, with the earlier needle-like contrast no longer resolved, indicating progression of the α → β-Mn transformation (compare 575 °C/1 h where elongated/needle-like contrast remained)

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, EBSD phase maps were acquired only for 525 °C/10 h, 575 °C/6 h and 650 °C/10 h (Fig. 5); no EBSD phase-fraction value is reported specifically for the 575 °C/3 h condition of this sample.

The XRD pattern of the 17Al alloy was recorded after aging at 575 °C for 1 h (Fig. 10, red trace) rather than for the 575 °C/3 h condition; both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks were found together with α/D0₃, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitation before full α → β-Mn transformation.

β-Mn precipitation kinetics context for the 17Al alloy: the α → β-Mn transformation was essentially complete after 6 h at 550 °C, and after only 1 h at 600 °C and above; at 575 °C it was complete at 6 h, so the 575 °C/3 h condition of this sample lies in a partially transformed regime (Fig. 5 / citing text).

The solution-treated baseline Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) is 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3, merged cell), which is the starting hardness before the 575 °C/3 h aging.
